q: A feeder supplies three motors with full-load currents of 20 A, 15 A and 10 A. The minimum feeder conductor ampacity is:
explain: 125% of the largest motor plus 100% of the others: 20 × 1.25 + 15 + 10 = 50 A.

q: A 25 hp, 460 V three-phase motor (Table FLC 34 A) requires branch-circuit copper conductors (75°C) of at least:
For the same 25 hp, 460 V motor (FLC 34 A), the maximum dual-element time-delay fuse for short-circuit and ground-fault protection is:
explain: Dual-element time-delay fuse: 175% × 34 = 59.5 A → 60 A standard size (next size up permitted by 430.52(C)(1) Exception 1).

q: A continuous-duty motor has a nameplate FLA of 32 A and a service factor of 1.15. The maximum overload relay setting is:
explain: 125% of nameplate for SF 1.15 or greater: 32 × 1.25 = 40 A. Use nameplate current, not the table value, for overloads.

q: A 45 kVA transformer (secondary 208Y/120 V, 125 A full load) is protected on both primary and secondary. The maximum secondary OCPD is:
explain: Secondary (9 A or more): 125% → 156 A; Note 1 permits the next higher standard rating, 175 A. With secondary protection in place the primary may be up to 250%.

q: A 75 kVA, 480 V three-phase transformer (primary current ≈ 90 A) is protected on the primary only. The maximum primary OCPD is:
A motor has a table full-load current of 28 A. A non-horsepower-rated disconnect switch for it must have an ampere rating of at least:
explain: 115% × 28 = 32.2 A — so in practice a 35 A (or larger) switch, or a horsepower-rated switch of adequate rating.

q: Conductors supplying a capacitor bank must have an ampacity of at least what percentage of the capacitor's rated current?
explain: 135% of rated current, to allow for harmonic currents and capacitance tolerance.

q: An AC general-use snap switch may serve as the disconnecting means for a motor rated 2 hp or less and 300 V or less, provided the motor's full-load current does not exceed what percentage of the switch rating?
explain: 80% of the switch's ampere rating. (A general-use switch rated at least twice the motor FLC is the other common permission for stationary motors ≤ 2 hp.)

q: The branch-circuit short-circuit and ground-fault protective device for a hermetic refrigerant motor-compressor shall not exceed what percentage of the rated-load current (unless needed for starting)?
explain: 175% of RLA or branch-circuit selection current; may go to 225% where the compressor won't start otherwise. The nameplate 'maximum fuse/breaker' marking governs when present.

q: Per Table 430.248, the full-load current of a 2 hp, 230 V single-phase motor is:
explain: 230 V single-phase: 1 hp → 8 A, 1½ hp → 10 A, 2 hp → 12 A, 3 hp → 17 A, 5 hp → 28 A. Halve the 115 V values.

q: Table 430.52 gives a maximum of 250% for an inverse-time breaker. For a motor with 14 A FLC, 250% = 35 A, which is a standard size. If the calculation had produced a non-standard value, the Code permits:
choices: Rounding down to the next standard size only
Using the next higher standard size
explain: Exception 1 allows the next higher standard rating when the computed value doesn't correspond to a standard size. Exception 2 allows further increases (up to 400% for breakers ≤ 100 A) only when needed to start the motor.
